name: Declarative codebase: every widget and component written in the one syntax
description:
Approved by Antonio 2026-11-18 after a review showed much of the UI code built imperatively.

THE SYNTAX (what was established — the rule every item of this feature is brought to):
```rust
Component::new()
    .prop_a(..)                                    // its own typed properties, as builders
    .child(
        Grid::new()
            .template_row("auto 1fr")              // the arrangement is a track template
            .child([header, body]),                // children in order, composed to any depth
    )
    .on_click(|ev| ev.dispatch(Intent::new("an_action")))   // behaviour lives on the widget
```
Declarative and nested in one expression, Flutter/SwiftUI-shaped, DOM-shaped events. NEVER: find a child by position (children[0]), write a style/bound/position by hand, rebuild a widget to change one property, put a number in the code. If something cannot be written in this shape, the library is missing a builder — propose it (RULE ZERO), never work around it.
- Children list bound to data: the declarative form (ForEach / map-like, e.g. `.child(items.map(..))` reconciled by key) is NOT in the library yet. Keyed (docs/widgets.md:5743), on_props / set_props / reconcile_keyed (:5767) exist but are low-level and imperative (Keyed is host-only) — they are not the authoring form; a declarative API on top must be proposed and approved first.
- Props that change over time need a signal-bound form; many widgets lack it (e.g. Input placeholder/value).
- Behaviour: one click path for every activatable widget, every event reachable by plugins — owned by P087(F011)/T565 (approved plan in that task).
- heca-pro: the API it builds on (F012 surface) stays compatible — new form beside the old, removal agreed; heca-pro follows the same syntax.

WHERE IT IS WRITTEN (references):
- CLAUDE.md — "⭐ THE SYNTAX" block at the top (loaded in every session).
- AGENTS.md § 0 — "⭐ THE SYNTAX" and "⭐ heca-pro builds on heca — keep its API compatible, and it follows the same syntax".
- docs/widgets.md — "⭐ THE SYNTAX" block before "Mental model".
- Existing examples of the shape: docs/layout.md:35, :109, :143 ("The one rule"); docs/widgets.md:2342, :2360, :5683, :7029-7030 (.child([a, b])).
- heca-pro/AGENTS.md — "⭐ THE SYNTAX" section (written 2026-11-18, committed by Antonio).
- Project decisions: 05a2ed0c (the syntax), 15ec67fc (heca-pro compatibility + same syntax).
- PR #322 (merged 2026-11-18) put the blocks into CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, docs/widgets.md.

CURRENT STATE (grep scan on main 2026-11-18, indicative only — the full review is step 1):
- Library widgets with children found by position: dialog 13, input 9, tree_layout 6, overlay 5, tile 4, command_palette 3, flex 3, resizable 3, message_list 2, tag 2, visibility 2.
- Library widgets positioning by hand (bounds writes / shift_subtree): command_palette 4, select 4, overlay 2, context_menu 2, scroll_region 2 (scroll_region/motion.rs:66), scroll_bar 2, toast 2, marker_group 2, badge_button 1, flex 1.
- Many numeric literals: key_hint 18, overlay 16, button 13, item 11, command_palette 11; Pane padding 8.0 (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/pane/mod.rs:60).
- App: terminal component lays itself out by writing style fields (heca/src/chrome/panes/terminal/component/mod.rs:103-108; search/mod.rs:218-220, focus by index :267); chrome/window; sidebar spots (providers/workspaces/column_group.rs:137 writes bounds; row_lines.rs:228, pane_row.rs:552 children by index); heca/src/components 6 index reads; the command palette (P087(F011)/T469, paused, uncommitted rewrite in heca-feat-469 still imperative).
- Described plugins have only press/change/toggle events (docs/widgets.md:7259).

PLAN (agreed):
1. Read-only review of every library widget (~60) and every app component against THE SYNTAX: per item, defects with file:line and a verdict (ok / fix / rewrite). Then one task per item, created with Antonio's consent.
2. Library first: declarative child list (proposal first), signal-bound props where needed, T565. Most-used widgets first (dialog, input, overlay, select, scroll_region, flex, tree_layout, tile, button, command_palette), then app (terminal, window, sidebar, palette).
3. Each item: done by the orchestrator without sub-agents, reviewed line by line against THE SYNTAX before Antonio's eye-check, one PR each.
ESTIMATE (2026-11-18, before the review): ~40–80 hours of work + 25–35 PRs to eye-check (~6–12 full days), revised after step 1.

acceptedDecisions.title: A property that changes is bound in the builder, never set on a built widget
acceptedDecisions.decision: Every builder property accepts either a fixed value or a value that changes (a Signal), under the same name and in the same place in the chain — THE SYNTAX unchanged. Whoever wants the property to change changes the STATE, never the widget: `let name = signal(..); Label::new(name); name.set(..)`. Layout and paint follow by themselves. This applies to every widget property AND to Base's style (layout and visual). It is the same model `.child(rooms.map(RoomRow::new))` (T569) already uses for children. Agreed with Antonio 2026-11-19 ("Sì").
acceptedDecisions.rationale:
Reaching into a built widget to set something (`label.text_signal().set(..)`, `row.state().set(true)`) is the imperative form; it is not THE SYNTAX, and it forced side tables of handles keyed by id. Flutter/SwiftUI bind a property to state where the property is written.

SHAPE DECIDED (Antonio, 2026-11-19, "Forma 1"): in native code the property itself accepts the signal — `Label::new(name)`, `.active(active)`, `.template_column(cols)` — the same builder takes a fixed value or a Signal. Not a separate `.bind("prop", signal)` next to the property (form 2, rejected for native code: the property written twice, its name a string that a typo breaks only at run time). Described plugins (ViewNode, WASM/RPC) cannot hold a signal and keep T360's `.text("Running").bind("text", "daemon_status")`; `realize` turns that binding into form 1 by passing the value store's signal to the builder (`Label::new(signal)`). So a described plugin is written the same whichever native form; a native plugin (heca-pro, heca::extension) writes form 1.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Library: one "value or signal" mechanism written once (no per-widget copy), every builder takes it; the layout engine records the signals a widget reads while measured (heca-grid-ui/src/layout/build.rs: apply_bound / remeasure / taffy_style / measure_text) and asks for layout when one changes; paint likewise. Then the window uses heca_grid_ui::needs_layout (the contract already documented in docs/widgets.md § "Asking the host to lay the tree out again") instead of laying out every frame — see project decision 06ac6e43 for why that was not done in T572.

acceptedDecisions.title: Base's fields stay public, like a DOM element's
acceptedDecisions.decision: `Base`'s fields (style, children, the visible/disabled/focused signals) stay public — heca and heca-pro use them the way a DOM element's properties are used. No field is made private to enforce layout updates. Antonio 2026-11-19: "heca-pro dovrebbe poter usare campi come si fa in un DOM element. non vedo perche' debbano essere privati."
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Rejected proposals of the same day: making style/children private behind methods, and a wrapper type that notices writes. The library already has the contract for structural changes (docs/widgets.md § needs_layout: mark_needs_layout, set_hidden guarded by a test); changing properties goes through bound signals (the decision above), so no field needs hiding.

acceptedDecisions.title: How a widget property changes today — three ways, two of them to remove (review of 2026-11-19)
acceptedDecisions.decision: Found in the code on 2026-11-19, to be brought to the bound form: (1) the widget keeps the signal and the caller takes the handle out after building it, storing it in side tables keyed by id — `ChromeSignals` (heca/src/chrome/window/signals.rs:26: pane_active, pane_previous, col_active, ws_active, ws_previous, row nav…) then `.set(..)` — imperative and a registry, against RULE ZERO: TO REMOVE; (2) the window tree is rebuilt when a state fingerprint changes (`chrome_signature`, heca/src/chrome/window/retained) — changing a property by rebuilding, against THE SYNTAX; also the source of ~19 ms layout spikes: TO REMOVE; (3) a builder takes the signal directly (`with_text_signal`, `with_max_lines_signal`, `with_mode_signal` — 13 uses) plus `.child(signal.map(..))`: the right form, to make the only one.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Inventory of the 56 widgets in heca-grid-ui (.planner/docs/f013-widget-properties-2026-11-19.md): 77 properties live (signals); ~110 widget properties fixed at construction; all of Base.style is plain fields nothing follows; ~120 fields are internal state (not properties). 22 widgets have no live property of their own, among them the ones that give the shape: Flex, Grid, Surface, Card, Pane, Overlay, Dialog, Button. Flex/Surface/Card/Tile/Panel/KeyHint/Tooltip/TreeLayout have no own properties — what they are is Base.style. Heaviest fixed ones: Grid template (columns, rows, areas), Button label/variant/glyph/active, Overlay position/panel_size/blocking, Pane frame/border, Label align/color/truncate, Row marker/colours, ScrollRegion axes/scrollbars/follow_bottom.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: This inventory is the "properties" part of F013 step 1 (the read-only review); the rest of step 1 (children by position, hand positioning, numeric literals, per-item verdict) is still to do. Proposed order (not yet confirmed by Antonio): Base.style first (unlocks every container at once), then Grid and Button, then the rest. Estimate for the properties part, agent time: value-or-signal mechanism + engine tracking 2–3 h; Base.style bindable ~2–3 h; ~110 widget properties with a test each 6–10 h; heca moved to the bound form (ChromeSignals tables and chrome_signature rebuilds gone, window uses needs_layout) 6–10 h; docs 1–2 h — ~17–28 h over several sessions, plus Antonio's eye-checks after Base, after the widgets, at the end. The F013 description's line "the declarative child list is NOT in the library yet" is outdated: T569 added `.child(items.map(..))`.

acceptedDecisions.title: AGENTS.md's SETTLED row shows the imperative form as the example — to correct
acceptedDecisions.decision: AGENTS.md (⭐ SETTLED table, the row "Then move ViewNode down into the library?", line ~1428) and docs/widget-architecture.md § 2 cite `row.state().set(true)` and `label.text_signal().set(…)` as how the native chrome updates in place. Their purpose there is to defend signals against routing everything through ViewNode, not to show how to write a widget — but they present the imperative form as the model, and nowhere in AGENTS.md is the bound form shown, so it got copied. To correct to the bound form (`Label::new(name)` with name a Signal; `.child(rooms.map(..))`; change the state, not the widget) — only after Antonio has gone through it ("Non modificare. Devi capire." 2026-11-19: a first edit was reverted).
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Agents copy the examples they see; the only example of an update after construction in the file every agent reads is the imperative one.

acceptedDecisions.title: T360 is the plugin half of the same work and depends on bindable native properties
acceptedDecisions.decision: P085(F003)/T360 (a per-mount value store a plugin writes, and `ViewNode` bindings `.text("Running").bind("text", "daemon_status")`) binds a described property by binding "the widget's signal". It can bind only properties that have a signal — 77 today. So F013's bound properties come first; T360 then uses them. No new task and no widening of T360 for the native work: it belongs to F013 (Antonio, 2026-11-19).
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Keeps one owner per capability: F013 owns native bindable properties and the bound form; T360 owns the described/plugin side and the value store.

acceptedDecisions.title: Floating panels are moved by hand after layout — the layout must place them (found on the tooltip, T567 point 23/23b)
acceptedDecisions.decision: Found 2026-11-19 while making the tooltip bubble a composed tree (P110(F010)/T567 points 23/23b): every floating panel is laid out somewhere, then moved to its place by hand, piece by piece — `shift_subtree` (heca-grid-ui/src/component/tree.rs) used by the tooltip, Select, ContextMenu, Overlay, ToastStack, CommandPalette, Flex, ScrollRegion. The positions the layout wrote and the final ones differ, so anything that remembers a position can be wrong; the same family of bug cut the tooltip's Tag in half during the eye-check. Decided with Antonio: fix it in F013, for every floating panel at once, not only the tooltip. The shape discussed: the panel declares where it wants to be — beside an anchor rect, on a preferred side, flipping when there is no room and kept inside the window (the rule that today lives in `place_beside`, heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/overlay/place.rs) — and the LAYOUT ENGINE measures it and writes the final positions once; nothing moves it afterwards, so drawing, clicking and repaint regions read true positions. This is CSS anchor positioning. NAME NOT DECIDED: I proposed `.beside(anchor, side)`; Antonio has never heard that word and prefers the CSS vocabulary — "position", "anchor" (e.g. a `position`/`anchor` builder). Agree the name with him before code.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: A panel's place depends on its own size (to centre it on the anchor, to flip it), so it cannot be decided by the caller before layout nor fixed up after without the two positions disagreeing; only the engine has both answers at the same moment.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Related existing builder: `LayoutExt::at_rect(..)` (heca-grid-ui/src/builders/layout.rs:108, CSS `position: absolute` + insets, the `Placement` type in style/length.rs:210). Antonio hoped it is internal: it is NOT — it is a public LayoutExt builder, and heca's app code uses it to place things by hand (heca/src/chrome/panes/terminal/viewport.rs, terminal/search/mod.rs, panes/column/shell.rs, surfaces/expose/workspace_row.rs, plus tests) — review those under F013 too. The anchored placement would be built on the same engine support (absolute position) plus the side choice. Tooltip bubble today: heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/tooltip.rs `place_bubble` (lay out, place_beside, shift_subtree).

acceptedDecisions.title: Widget glows written as numbers — derive them from the theme's glow, keeping each widget's own multiplier
acceptedDecisions.decision: Found 2026-11-19 (T567 points 23/23b): many widgets write their halo's radius and intensity as numbers in code (`radius: 10.0`, `GLOW_RADIUS`, `GLOW_REST_INTENSITY`…). Grep count of such lines in heca-grid-ui/src/widgets: button/component.rs 11, row.rs 8, badge_button.rs 8, toggle.rs 7, scroll_bar.rs 5, checkbox.rs 5, badge.rs 5, tabs.rs 4, status_dot.rs 4, rail_cell.rs 4, progress.rs 4, marker_group.rs 4, icon_button.rs 4, dock_frame.rs 4, select 5, button/mod.rs 3, toast 2, tag 2, spinner 2, scroll_region 4, pane 2, item 2, gauge 2 (indicative). The fix, as for the tooltip: the halo comes from the theme's glow (active_glow_radius / active_glow_strength, the user's `glow_size` GlowLevel on top via PaintCx::scaled_glow) — NOT one same halo for every widget: Antonio, 2026-11-19: "lo stesso alone non va bene per tutti, molti usano un moltiplicatore da applicare a quel valore e questo va tenuto". Each widget keeps its own relative strength, expressed as a multiplier on the theme value (or a named GlowLevel like the tooltip's Thin), never an absolute number.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: An absolute radius/intensity in a widget ignores the theme and drifts from the other widgets; but flattening every halo to one token would erase deliberate differences (a resting control is faint, an active one strong). A multiplier on the theme value keeps both.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Verify widget by widget before changing: which numbers are already multipliers on a theme value (keep them as they are), which are absolute (turn into a multiplier on the theme glow so the look stays the same at the default theme), and that the default look does not change (compare with the showcase). Done for the tooltip in T567: heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/tooltip.rs uses `active_glow_radius * GlowLevel::Thin.radius_scale()` and `active_glow_strength * GlowLevel::Thin.strength_scale()`.

acceptedDecisions.title: Wrappers take their child in the constructor — bring them to `Wrapper::new().prop(..).child(..)` (Visibility done in T567)
acceptedDecisions.decision: Raised by heca-pro (2026-11-20) and agreed by Antonio: a wrapper whose constructor takes the child (and sometimes an unnamed positional value) does not follow THE SYNTAX. Visibility was changed in P110(F010)/T567 (2026-11-20) to `Visibility::new().visible(bool).child(c)` — `new(child, bool)` removed, every heca call site moved, heca-pro adapts its own. TO DO, same shape: KeyHint::new(child) (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/key_hint/mod.rs:59), KeyHintGroup::new(child) (key_hint_group.rs:103), FocusScope::new(child) (focus_scope/mod.rs:53), Tooltip::new(child, text) / Tooltip::new_signal(child, text) (tooltip.rs:318, :323) → `X::new().<props>.child(c)`. Antonio's word for these: change the constructor directly (as Visibility), heca-pro adapts its code; tell heca-pro when each lands.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Every container takes children with `.child(..)`; a wrapper that takes its child as a constructor argument is a second shape, and a positional bool (`Visibility::new(x, true)`) says nothing at the call site. Rust cannot keep two `new` with different arguments, so the old form cannot stay beside the new one under the same name; Antonio chose the direct change because heca-pro asked for it.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Pattern to copy: heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/visibility.rs (new() empty, property builders, `child` replaces the one child and calls component::wrap_transparently; apply/paint walk the children instead of reading the first by position). The layout side of transparent wrappers (a wrapper lays its child out as the child's real parent would) was fixed centrally in T567 in heca-grid-ui/src/layout/build.rs, test heca-grid-ui/tests/transparent_wrapper.rs.

acceptedDecisions.title: Icon and Image are sized only in pixels — they need a theme-relative size
acceptedDecisions.decision: Found 2026-11-20 (T567, review of the DockFrame/Row work): `Icon::size(px: f32)` (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/icon.rs:371) is the only way to size an icon, and it shadows LayoutExt's theme-relative `.size(WidgetSize)`; so DockFrame's rail icon is a pixel constant (dock_frame.rs RAIL_ICON_SIZE = 22.0) and showcase/app code writes icon sizes as numbers. `Image` has no theme-relative size either: the agent line sizes its logo by hand with `.width(cx.theme.font_size).height(cx.theme.font_size)` (heca/src/providers/workspaces/agent_line/mod.rs). Wanted: both take a size from the theme (a step relative to the font, like WidgetSize / Spacing), and the pixel form is no longer the way to write it. Not fixed in T567 because it is a public API change whose name and shape must be agreed with Antonio (and heca-pro, decision 15ec67fc).
acceptedDecisions.rationale: A size written at the call site (a number, or a theme value read where it is consumed) is the 'nothing written by hand' rule broken; the library is missing the builder (RULE ZERO).
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Check every `Icon::new(..).size(` and Image `.width/.height` with a theme value in heca, heca-renderer showcase and heca-pro when doing it.

acceptedDecisions.title: Every widget is customizable like an HTML element — a widget whose look cannot be overridden is a defect
acceptedDecisions.decision: Antonio, 2026-11-20: every widget — composed ones included (Item, ItemGroup, Tag, Card, Select…) — must be customizable the way an HTML element is: its padding, margins, colours, borders, radius, alignment overridable by its builders/style (a hand style wins over the variant's look, as Row's RowVariant does). A widget that "brings its own look" which cannot be changed is not a reason to avoid it; it is a defect to fix under F013. Part of F013 step 1's review: for each widget, list what of its look cannot be overridden today.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Raised while discussing AGENTS.md's step 3 ("never use a ready-made composite as the layout … they have their own look"), added by me on 2026-11-19 in be00a420 (PR #329, T570) copying heca-pro's steps without pointing it out to Antonio. Antonio: "devono essere customizzabili tutti come un elemento html. se non lo sono vanno fixati in F013."
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: The AGENTS.md step 3 wording ("Never use a ready-made composite as the layout") reads as a ban and is to be reworded only as Antonio decides (he edits AGENTS.md policy; I do not change it unasked).

acceptedDecisions.title: The active-marker bar and pip are pixel sizes in three widgets — the theme needs one token for them
acceptedDecisions.decision: Found 2026-11-20 while bringing Item's spaces to theme steps (T567): the width of the vivid left bar that marks the active row is a pixel constant written separately in Item (ACTIVE_BAR_W = 3.0, heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/item.rs), Row (its own bar width, row.rs) and MarkerGroup (BAR_W / BAR_W_HOVER, marker_group.rs:210); Item's selected-option pip is CHECK_SIZE = 10.0. Three copies of one look means the theme is missing a token (marker bar width, and pip size relative to the font); add it once and read it in all three. Not done in T567: a theme field is an API change to agree with Antonio.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Spaces in Item now come from theme steps (Spacing); these two shapes have no theme value to come from, and inventing a Spacing step for a line width would be the wrong unit.

acceptedDecisions.title: A dock is a trait (Provider), not a component in THE SYNTAX — bring it to `Dock::new(id).title(..).child(..)`
acceptedDecisions.decision: Found 2026-11-20 (T567 C32, dock config): a dock is written by implementing the `Provider` trait (heca/src/providers/mod.rs) — its properties are trait METHODS (`id`, `kind`, `title`, `supported_regions`, `default_region`, `movable`, `collapsible`, and `spawn`, which I added on 2026-11-20 copying that shape instead of flagging it), and its content is built in a closure (`build_contribution` → `ContainerContribution::new(self, |ctx, build| widget)`). THE SYNTAX wants a component with builders: `Dock::new("rooms").title("Rooms").regions(RegionSet::SIDEBARS).spawnable(..).child(content)`, added with `regions("sidebar.right").append(|| Dock::new(..)…)`. `regions(name).append/remove/retain` itself stays a function on purpose (a region is a list every plugin appends to, fetched by name — chrome/docks/regions.rs module docs) — that part is not a defect. The change touches every dock, heca-pro's included (decision 15ec67fc: new form beside the old, removal agreed).
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Antonio, 2026-11-20: "ma perché non me lo segnali??? devo dirtelo io??????" — the non-conformance was known to me while I extended the trait and I did not say it.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Step already taken in T567: `default_region()` gets a trait default and is deprecated (nothing in the app reads it; only tests and a copy in ContainerContribution nobody reads). Also from today's work, still imperative inside the library: DockFrame::build_toggle rebuilds the title row by swapping children found by area name (part_mut / area_slot / mem::replace) instead of binding a declarative row to state; Item paints its active bar (3px) and pip (10px) by hand (F013 decision bf271be6).

acceptedDecisions.title: Docks and regions reachable from anywhere at runtime — a handle by id, index reads, any thread
acceptedDecisions.decision: Antonio, 2026-11-20: from any part of the code — heca, an extension, a plugin — one imports `heca::regions(..)` (like a singleton) and operates on regions AND on docks at any time. State on 2026-11-20 (main after PR #333): `regions(name).append / prepend / remove(id, any region) / retain / gap` work at runtime, applied each frame. MISSING, to build here: (1) a handle to an existing dock by id, reachable from anywhere — e.g. `regions(..).get("rooms")` / returned by `append` — whose methods act through the host (move, remove, change properties such as the title), valid across a remake of the dock because it holds the id, not the object; (2) index-based access (Antonio's example `at_index(n)`): decide reading the dock at position n (safe) vs inserting at n (fragile: a plugin inserting shifts every later index, which is why regions.rs avoids indexes and offers `.order(..)`); (3) `regions(..)` from any thread: today its queue is `thread_local!` (heca/src/chrome/docks/regions.rs), so a call from a background thread or from an extension's server-side service lands in a queue nobody reads and is lost silently — make one queue the window reads, and calls from the server reach the windows. Names (`get`, `at_index`, handle methods) to be agreed with Antonio before code; heca-pro is told (decision 15ec67fc).
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Antonio asked for regions usable at runtime ("region('name').append().remove().get().at_index() etc.. da potere richiamare in ogni momento anche dai plugins") and for the same on providers ("deve essere possibile avere un riferimento e chiamare i suoi metodi"). The append/remove half landed in PR #333; nothing in the planner covered handles, index access or the thread limit (searched 2026-11-20).
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Goes with decision a7f74a7c (the dock as a `Dock::new(..)` component): the handle's methods are that component's properties, applied through the host. Host side today: ChromeHost::apply_pending (heca/src/chrome/docks/host/placing.rs) applies the queue every frame from handle_about_to_wait; ChromeHost::provider(id) is the internal lookup. WASM plugins need the adapter of P022(F003)/T075 for any of this.
